1.note: Read as Basra in Iraq, a trading city. The same spelling is biblical Bozrah (Isa 34:6, 63:1).

2.note: The words of the burnt-offering law (Lev 1:9, "its entrails and its legs he shall wash in water"): the fallen traveler is washed like a sacrifice.

3.note: Num 14:24 says this in praise of Caleb; here it means that the sea makes him another man, out of his mind with fear.

4.he: וּבֵיתָהּ תַּחֲשֹׁב מַאְסָר וְנוּדָהּ / מְבַשֵּׂר טוֹב
4.note: The restless soul counts home a prison and wandering good news, so it never stops. Both poems of the gate end with the same half-line from Isa 52:7.

5.note: A pun on the name: חֶבֶר (Ḥever) and מְחַבֵּר (one who joins; also "author").
